clauses.reason: Executive Order 6684-C of April 19, 1934 states: "do order that the said Electrical Contracting Chapter be and it is hereby approved, and that the previous approval of said Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry is hereby modified to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as modified by the addition thereto of said Electrical Contracting Chapter". That command is an approval of the Electrical Contracting Chapter of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry and a modification of the earlier approval of that code to cover the code as supplemented under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and it has legal effect only through that approval: under section 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, and under sections 3(c) and 3(f) violations were restrainable in equity and punishable as misdemeanors. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no other effective date, so the command ended as a prospective operative command on June 14, 1935. No earlier end is shown (see earlier_end_check). The June 16, 1935 expiry is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6684-C (April 19, 1934) is an approval of the Electrical Contracting Chapter of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry, and a modification of the earlier approval of that code to cover the code as supplemented, under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362453), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Identity and page check: the page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2025-12-08T01:28:26Z whose heading names Executive Order 6684-C, whose date (April 19, 1934) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The census register and the WPA 1944 list (1934 Apr 19, p.575, approval of the code for the Electrical Contracting Division of the Construction Industry) give the same date and subject. The order's own text states no limit on the approval. Its command depends entirely on the code approval, so its first end is the repeal of the code-approval and code-enforcement provisions of Title I by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935, applying SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and its adjudication; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization only.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no period, \"until\" date, condition or provisional approval that limits the approval, and no stay or postponement to a fixed date. The Construction Industry Code was approved January 31, 1934 (EO 6578). A scan of the held 1933-1935 order titles and a text search for \"Construction Industry\" find, besides EO 6578 and this order, the approvals of sibling chapters and subchapters (EO 6606-D, 6640, 6684-E, 6711-B, 6750-B, 6988-A, 7025-A), EO 6731-A (June 6, 1934), EO 6925-A (December 19, 1934), and many orders of September 1934 to May 1935 approving agreements between members of divisions of the code (EO 6860-A through EO 7036-D by title). I read the operative sentence of EO 6731-A and of each of the seven chapter approvals. Each chapter approval approves a further chapter or subchapter and modifies or amends the parent approval to include the code as supplemented; none cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes the Electrical Contracting Chapter or the parent code. EO 6711-B reserves review of, and stays or exemptions from, one section of the plumbing chapter, and EO 6988-A and 7025-A reserve review of a section on mutual agreements with a possible stay of that section; a stay of one section would not end the approval of this chapter. EO 6731-A is a different command: it appoints Sullivan W. Jones as chairman of the National Construction Planning and Adjustment Board during the pleasure of the Administrator, and it does not touch this approval. EO 6925-A cancels the order approving a different code (the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade) and names the Construction Industry Code only as the code that would govern that trade's construction operations after the cancellation. I read the operative sentence of the five held orders approving agreements of the Electrical Contracting Division (EO 6883-B, 6892-A, 6974-A, 6984-A and 7010-F): each approves an agreement and none cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes this chapter. I did not read the other agreement orders; by title they approve agreements among members of code divisions and are separate instruments that this analysis does not decide, and none is titled as a cancellation of the code. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or revoked before June 14, 1935, and none shows a modification under section 10(b) that reached this order's command. June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.","independent_command_check":"No appointment, delegation, direction to a government agency, report direction or other command independent of the code approval appears. The \"Approval Recommended\" line and the signature line command nothing.","savings_check":"Read S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and its proviso and NIRA section 5 in the packet excerpts. No held source continues this approval, a prosecution under it or any command of this order after June 14, 1935; accrued acts, liabilities and the section 5 exemption for completed action are recorded as transferred or accrued and not as continued operation.","scope_check":"One operative command with two parts that depend on each other: approval of the Electrical Contracting Chapter and modification of the previous approval of the Construction Industry Code to include that code as supplemented. Both act only through the section 3 approval of the code as supplemented, so one clause covers them."}

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, and the section 5 exemption from the antitrust laws for action complying with an approved code taken while Title I was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for completed action. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action under them, not codes, and states no time limit; the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the section 5 exemption for past action under codes, and whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this approval. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935: the Court held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the Live Poultry Code provisions in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization for every section 3 code approval, not as this order's end; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 3; the provisions described were repealed on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2).
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3 (48 Stat. 195, June 16, 1933): under 3(a) the President approved codes and could impose conditions of approval; under 3(b), 3(c) and 3(f) an approved code's provisions became standards of fair competition enforceable by injunction and as misdemeanors. These are the legal effects that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 5; S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935) limited the exemption by proviso; the held text does not settle the proviso's effect on past action.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 5 exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under Title I and any complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days thereafter; any exemption for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
